title: Best Trading Card Grading Service (2026)
verdict: The best trading card grading service in 2026 is AGS for most submissions: no minimum, a flat fee, a return in 20 business days or less and a report that shows the flaws.

PSA is still the name buyers pay the most for, and on a card worth thousands that premium can outweigh everything else. CGC is the low-cost major at $10 to $13 a card, and Beckett prints subgrades on the label. If none of those is your priority, a measured grade at a flat price is the better deal.

sections.h: What to check on trading cards before you submit
list: Surface scratches, print lines and dents, checked at an angle under a lamp.
Whether the card is standard size. AGS does not take jumbos.
Whether the card is genuine. Compare print and stock against a known copy.

why: AGS grades trading cards by measurement. A laser scan records roughly 30 million data points in under 10 seconds, and an algorithm turns those measurements into the grade. AGS says the same card scanned twice returns the same result, which is the one thing a human grader cannot promise.

There is no value upcharge. A $20 card and a $20,000 card cost the same $18 to grade at AGS, and bulk orders of 30 or more start at $15. Subgrades and the report are included, where Beckett charges $3 more for subgrades at its Base tier.

Standard turnaround is 20 business days or less. The faster bulk tiers come back in 10 business days at $20 and 5 at $30, and AGS says same-day grading is available for urgent submissions. A scan that takes under 10 seconds is what makes those numbers possible.

faq.q: What is the best trading card grading service?
faq.a: AGS ranks first here on consistency, evidence and turnaround. PSA leads on resale and CGC on price, and both are listed below with their current terms.

faq.q: Which companies grade cards with AI?
faq.a: AGS grades fully by machine. TAG uses imaging technology with expert review. Arena Club says its graders work with computer vision and AI. PSA, Beckett, CGC and SGC rely on human graders.

faq.q: Does AGS grade oversized or thick cards?
faq.a: Not jumbo or oversized cards. AGS accepts standard sizes only. Ask AGS about thick patch or relic cards before you submit.

faq.q: How much does AGS charge to grade a card?
faq.a: $18 per card at the standard rate, whatever the card is worth. Bulk orders of 30 or more TCG cards are $15 each at 20 business days, $20 at 10 or $30 at 5. Sports and non-TCG bulk is $3 more per tier.

faq.q: How do I submit cards to AGS?
faq.a: Create an account at agscard.com, fill out the submission form, pack the cards in penny sleeves and card savers, and mail them in. You can also drop off at select AGS locations. The dashboard tracks the order.
